title: The larynx: breathing, voice and airway protection
intro: The larynx sits between the throat and windpipe. It lets air pass, produces voice and helps keep food out of the airway. Speaking and swallowing require coordinated muscles and nerves, not just a single moving flap.

sections.heading: Supporting framework
paragraphs: Cartilages support the larynx while allowing movement. Its lining is delicate; smoke, irritation and heavy voice use can affect it. A visible neck prominence does not measure voice health.

sections.heading: Making sound
paragraphs: Air from the lungs makes the vocal folds vibrate when positioned for speech. Their tension and vibration affect pitch; mouth and tongue shape sounds into words.

sections.heading: Swallowing
paragraphs: The larynx rises and several protective closures cooperate, including the epiglottis and vocal folds. Cough helps clear material, but repeated choking is not something to ignore.

sections.heading: Looking after voice
paragraphs: Avoid smoking and repeated shouting, take breaks and maintain suitable hydration. Persistent hoarseness needs examination rather than indefinite whispering or repeated unprescribed antibiotics.

sections.heading: Warning signs
paragraphs: Noisy or difficult breathing, inability to swallow saliva or rapidly increasing throat swelling requires urgent help. Coughing during meals or a lasting voice change needs assessment, particularly with weight loss or a neck lump.

A diagram explains typical structure, not the cause of an individual symptom. Before a consultation, note when a change began, what brings it on and how it affects daily activities. Bring previous results and ask how the findings fit together.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira loses her voice after heavy use. She rests it sensibly and arranges review if the change persists rather than forcing through performances.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben repeatedly coughs while drinking. He requests swallowing assessment instead of assuming it is harmless clumsiness.
